record.paper_title: A Nonequilibrium Statistical Ensemble Formalism. Maxent-Nesom: Concepts, Construction, Application, Open Questions and Criticisms
record.original_question: What is the precise relationship, and possible partial equivalence, between Prigogine's approach to irreversible statistical mechanics and the MaxEnt-NESOM treatment of irreversibility through Zubarev-style time smoothing, initial conditions, and retarded solutions of the Liouville equation?

evidence.quote: Certain kind of equivalence - at least partial - seems to exists between Prigogine's approach and MaxEnt-NESOM, as pointed out by Dougherty, and we side with Dougherty's view.
More recently, Prigogine and his School have extended those ideas incorporating concepts, at the quantum level, related to dynamical instability and chaos.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider two formal frameworks for describing irreversible processes in statistical mechanics.

(A) Prigogine's approach. One studies the Liouville equation
\[ i\,\partial_t\rho(t) = L\rho(t), \qquad L = \{H,\cdot\}_{PB}\ \text{(classical) or}\ [H,\cdot]/\hbar\ \text{(quantum)}, \]
and seeks a (generally non-unitary) similarity transformation \(\Lambda\) acting on the space of densities such that the transformed density \(\tilde\rho(t)=\Lambda\rho(t)\) satisfies a semigroup evolution
\[ \partial_t\tilde\rho(t) = -\Phi\,\tilde\rho(t),\qquad t\ge 0, \]
with \(\Phi\) generating a contractive semigroup, thereby producing intrinsic irreversibility and a monotonically increasing entropy functional. Extensions of this program incorporate dynamical instability, large Poincaré systems and quantum chaos.

(B) MaxEnt–NESOM (Zubarev-style nonequilibrium statistical operator method). One fixes a set of basic dynamical observables \(\{\hat P_j\}\) whose averages are taken as the macroscopic state variables, defines an auxiliary "instantaneous" generalized Gibbs distribution
\[ \bar\varrho(t) = \exp\!\Big(-\phi(t) - \sum_j F_j(t)\hat P_j\Big) \]
maximizing Gibbs entropy under the constraints \(\mathrm{Tr}\,[\bar\varrho(t)\hat P_j]=\langle \hat P_j\rangle(t)\), and then constructs the actual nonequilibrium statistical operator by Zubarev's time-smoothing prescription
\[ \varrho_\varepsilon(t) = \varepsilon\!\int_{-\infty}^{t} e^{\varepsilon(t'-t)}\,U(t,t')\bar\varrho(t')U^\dagger(t,t')\,dt',\qquad \varepsilon\to 0^+, \]
which is equivalent to selecting the retarded (Bogoliubov-quasi-averaged) solution of the Liouville equation under an initial condition imposed in the remote past.

Problem. Establish the precise mathematical relationship between frameworks (A) and (B). Specifically:

1. Construct, on a common functional-analytic setting (e.g.\ a rigged Hilbert space of densities with a chosen contraction semigroup structure), an explicit map between Prigogine's similarity operator \(\Lambda\) and the Zubarev time-smoothing/projection prescription that produces \(\varrho_\varepsilon(t)\); identify the class of Hamiltonians, observables \(\{\hat P_j\}\) and boundary conditions in the distant past for which the two prescriptions yield the same coarse-grained reduced dynamics for \(\langle\hat P_j\rangle(t)\) and the same entropy production.

2. Determine whether this equivalence is full or only partial: characterize the systems and observable algebras for which the Prigogine semigroup evolution coincides with the MaxEnt–NESOM evolution at the level of (i) the reduced density operator, (ii) the macroscopic transport equations, and (iii) the H-theorem and entropy production functional.

3. In the cases where exact equivalence fails, give a quantitative description of the discrepancy (e.g.\ in terms of the choice of basic observables, of the Bogoliubov infinitesimal source \(\varepsilon\), or of the spectral properties of \(L\) such as the existence of complex spectral decompositions associated with large Poincaré systems and quantum dynamical instability).
artifact.status_search_result: No published proof of a precise, rigorous equivalence between Prigogine's subdynamics/similarity approach and the Zubarev MaxEnt-NESOM construction has been located. The literature (e.g., Dougherty's commentaries, Luzzi–Vasconcellos–Ramos reviews) only argues for a partial conceptual equivalence, and the mathematical correspondence remains a stated open question.

status_evidence.title: A Nonequilibrium Statistical Ensemble Formalism (overview)
status_evidence.snippet: Describes the MaxEnt-NESOM formalism and lists relations to Prigogine's approach among open questions.
status_evidence.claim: The precise relation/equivalence is posed as an open question.
